results.reason: Issue 3 locates the one-sided assignment right in SA §13.2. It notes Supplier may assign without consent or notice while Customer cannot. It explains the risks to supply continuity and to confidential drawings and specifications. It recommends mutual consent, a competitor carve-out and notice, with proposed language.

Issue 1 identifies the §13.3 change of control consent requirement and the termination right. It ties both to the pending sale. It recommends deleting the clause, limiting it to competitors with consent not unreasonably withheld, or obtaining a waiver before signing or closing.
The memo never mentions the auto-renewal in OF §2.2 or the 30-day non-renewal notice lock-in risk. It cites only OF 2.1 for the Initial Term.
Issue 2 identifies that §9.3 carves Customer's §10.1 indemnity out of the cap while Supplier stays capped. It recommends deleting §9.3 or making the carve-out mutual and narrow.
The memo correctly states the 12-month fees cap (§9.1), Delaware law (§12.1), the March 1, 2026 Effective Date and the three-year Initial Term.
The memo states the SA > OF > Spec order of precedence (§1.3). It applies this to the change of control analysis and to the Spec.
The memo gives an explicit raise-first ordering and HIGH labels. Change of control is ranked #1 and the indemnity #2.
Each issue has Where, Why it matters and Recommended fix, with proposed language. A separate open questions and business decisions section appears at the end.
The memo expressly states the Spec has no problematic term. It cites no outside statutes or cases and invents no significant issues.
